GlobalForge Equipment Corp. - Q2 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalForge Equipment Corp. Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GlobalForge Equipment Corp.'s results for the Q2 FY2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Mitchell, Chief Financial Officer; and David Chen, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on GlobalForge Equipment Corp.'s performance for the Q2. We've made significant progress on several fronts, delivering another strong quarter that underscores the resilience and momentum in our core industrial equipment markets. We've achieved robust revenue growth fueled by healthy organic expansion, favorable product mix, and strategic pricing amid inflationary pressures on key raw materials like steel and aluminum alloys. Demand remains strong across key end markets, with standout order intake in construction, mining, and even resilience in agriculture despite some headwinds. Our book-to-bill ratios are expanding, backlog is at record levels providing excellent visibility, and we're navigating price-cost dynamics effectively to drive margin expansion. Operationally, we're advancing our Industry 4.0 initiatives, including AI-driven optimizations and electrification trends that are positioning us for sustained outperformance.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Mitchell (CFO):
Thank you, Johnathan. Good afternoon, everyone—thank you for joining our Q2 FY2024 earnings call for GlobalForge Equipment Corp. I'll dive right into our top-line performance and broader financials, where we delivered another strong quarter underscoring resilience across our industrial equipment markets.

For the second quarter, total revenue reached $1.52 billion, representing 12.8% year-over-year growth and marking our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit topline expansion. On a full-year basis through the first half of FY2024, we've now achieved $3.05 billion in revenue, up 11.5% from the prior-year period. This performance exceeded our guidance midpoint and reflects a healthy blend of organic growth at 10.2%, favorable product mix, and strategic pricing actions. The remainder came from our Q1 acquisition of Nordic Robotics, adding bolt-on automation capabilities without integration issues.

Breaking it down by segment, our Machinery division—including our flagship CNC machining centers, hydraulic presses, and automated assembly lines—generated $920 million, up 14.2% year-over-year. This was driven by robust demand for our next-gen PrecisionForge 5000 series, which incorporates advanced IoT-enabled predictive maintenance and AI-driven optimization, helping customers like automotive OEMs reduce downtime by up to 25%. Average selling prices, or ASPs, in this segment rose 4.1% due to a favorable mix shift toward higher-margin automation solutions, outpacing volume growth of 9.8%. Bookings in Machinery hit a record $1.1 billion, with backlog now standing at $4.2 billion, providing excellent visibility into FY2025.

Our Engine and Power Systems segment contributed $380 million, a solid 10.5% increase, fueled by aftermarket parts and services for heavy-duty diesel engines used in mining and construction applications. Electrification trends are accelerating here, with our new hybrid-electric propulsion units—similar to those pioneered by competitors like Cummins in their HELM platform—gaining traction. We shipped over 2,500 units in Q2, representing 15% of segment revenue, up from just 5% a year ago.

Finally, our Components and Distribution arm delivered $220 million, up 9.2%, benefiting from easing supply chain bottlenecks. We've seen lead times for critical forgings and castings compress from 16 weeks to under 10, thanks to our multi-sourcing strategy with suppliers in Mexico and Vietnam.

Regionally, North America remains our bedrock, accounting for 52% of revenue at $790 million, up 13.5% year-over-year, propelled by the U.S. infrastructure bill's $1.2 trillion spend on highways and manufacturing reshoring. Reshoring initiatives, akin to those boosting peers like Caterpillar in their domestic foundry expansions, have driven a 20% surge in orders from Midwest fab shops.

Asia-Pacific grew even faster at 18.2%, contributing 28% of total revenue or $425 million. China's stimulus package for semiconductor and EV manufacturing has supercharged demand for our high-precision grinding machines, while India's PLI scheme for steel and auto sectors mirrors the capex boom we saw in Deere's ag equipment last cycle. EMEA rounded out at 20% of revenue, up 8.7%, though tempered by softer German machinery orders amid energy transition headwinds.

Strategically, this growth is no accident. Our 12% YoY increase in R&D spend to $85 million in Q2—focused on Industry 4.0 integrations like edge computing for real-time vibration monitoring and sustainable alloys for net-zero compliance—positions us to capture share in a market projected by McKinsey to grow at 6-8% CAGR through 2030. We've also realized $45 million in procurement savings YTD via digital twin simulations for supply chain modeling, directly flowing to margins. Looking ahead, we see sustained tailwinds from capex recovery in oil & gas, where rig counts are up 15% per Baker Hughes data, and the global push for smart factories amid labor shortages.

Turning now to order intake, which continues to be a standout leading indicator for our business. In Q2, we delivered total order intake of $2.85 billion, marking a robust 28% year-over-year growth on an organic basis, excluding a modest 2% foreign exchange headwind from the strengthening USD. This not only exceeded our guidance range but also represents our strongest quarterly order intake since Q4 2022, during the peak of the post-pandemic capex rebound. Sequentially, orders were up 12% from Q1, underscoring sustained momentum across our end markets.

Breaking this down by key segments: Discrete Automation—our largest at 45% of intake—surged 42% YoY to $1.28 billion. Demand for our next-gen CNC machining centers and collaborative robot systems remains red-hot, fueled by semiconductor fab expansions from customers like TSMC and Intel. Our new AI-optimized spindle technology, launched earlier this year, has been a game-changer, reducing cycle times by up to 25% and winning us major orders from U.S.-based chipmakers reshoring production under the CHIPS Act.

Process Industries—30% of mix—grew 22% YoY to $855 million. Here, we're benefiting from energy transition plays, with strong bookings for our high-efficiency turbomachinery and heat exchanger systems. Notably, we secured a $150 million order for LNG compression equipment from a Middle Eastern EPC contractor, capitalizing on the global LNG buildout amid Europe's energy security push.

Aerospace & Defense—15% of intake—posted 18% YoY growth to $428 million, supported by aftermarket MRO demand and OEM ramp-ups. Our precision forging presses for titanium components are seeing pull-through from Boeing and Airbus supply chain recovery efforts. Other segments, including general industrial and mining equipment, rounded out at 15% YoY to $297 million.

Regionally, Americas (52% of intake) led with 35% YoY growth to $1.48 billion, driven by U.S. infrastructure spending via the IIJA and IRA bills. We're gaining share in data center cooling systems against competitors like Trane Technologies, with orders up 50% in that sub-vertical. EMEA (28%) grew 24% YoY to $799 million, resilient despite high energy costs and Ukraine conflict impacts, thanks to German automotive OEMs like Volkswagen investing in EV battery gigafactories—our modular skid-mounted assembly lines have shortened lead times to 16 weeks versus the industry average of 24. APAC (20%) rose 19% YoY to $571 million, with China stabilizing and India emerging strong on green steel initiatives via electric arc furnace melters.

This order strength has supercharged our order backlog to a record $9.2 billion, up 26% YoY and providing over 14 months of revenue visibility at current run rates. Aftermarket services now comprise 22% of intake.

Diving deeper into order intake and book-to-bill trends by end market—construction, mining, and agriculture—while weaving in regional nuances. Order intake reflects new bookings secured during the quarter, and book-to-bill is quarterly bookings divided by quarterly billings. A ratio above 1.0 signals backlog expansion.

Company-wide, Q2 order intake was that $2.85 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 8% sequentially. Book-to-bill expanded to 1.28x, up from 1.12x prior quarter and 1.05x a year ago, ballooning backlog to $12.4 billion, up 22% YoY, or over 14 months of visibility. Aftermarket parts and services, 28% of total intake, grew 18% YoY.

By end market: Construction (42% of bookings) surged 22% YoY to $1.2 billion, book-to-bill 1.45x. North American infrastructure via IIJA drove U.S. bookings up 31%, led by 20- to 40-ton excavator line including HX Series hybrids with 15% better fuel efficiency—we're gaining 2.5 share points per IRON data. EMEA flat amid German PMI softness, offset by UK/France growth on data centers/renewables; Asia-Pacific up 19%, India highways boosting compact track loaders. We're ramping electro-hydraulic initiatives like eHX prototypes for Tier 4 compliance.

Mining (31%) rose 9% YoY to $885 million, book-to-bill 1.22x. Copper/lithium demand lifted 150-300-tonne haul trucks 25%, including $250 million Andean deal for autonomous-ready MT300s. Australia (42% of mining) up 15% on gold/iron ore, with battery-electric prototypes via Rio Tinto yielding 20% uptime via IntelliMine AI. South Africa flat on platinum/load-shedding, offset by 24% aftermarket; $150 million Kalgoorlie investment for localized batteries targets Scope 3 cuts.

Agriculture (18%) dipped 4% YoY to $513 million, book-to-bill 1.05x, pressured by grain prices/farmer caution. North America (60%) flat, offset by 5% ASPs on PrecisionAg telematics tractors; Brazil up 18% on sprayers; Europe down 12% on fertilizers, countered by AgroBot rovers like John Deere precision. FarmConnect IoT subscriptions up 35%, now 15% of ag bookings. Others: Oil & gas up 16%, forestry 1.15x.

Regionally: North America 48% +19% YoY, 1.35x; EMEA 22% +3%, 1.18x; Asia-Pacific 21% +17%, 1.30x; LatAm 9% +8%, 1.20x.

These trends affirm 1.8 share points gained per McKinsey, via EdgeControl maintenance at 98% uptime. $300 million vertical integration protects deliveries; Peoria/Belo Horizonte at 92% utilization; Q3 bookings $2.9-3.1 billion implies full-year >1.25x.

On book-to-bill specifically, our consolidated ratio was 1.18x, up from 1.09x in Q1 and 15% better YoY from 1.03x. Strongest since Q4 2022, with bookings $1.42 billion (12% sequential, 22% YoY) outpacing $1.20 billion billings (8% YoY).

By segment: Aerospace & Defense 1.32x on $285 million, titanium 5-axis mills for Boeing/Lockheed, backlog $2.8 billion +18%. Automotive & EV 1.15x, $410 million battery die-casting, up 28%. Energy & Renewables 0.98x on $320 million, hydrogen/wind amid oil volatility. General Industrial 1.12x on packaging/semicon.

Regions: Americas 1.25x (52%, $740 million +25%) on CHIPS reshoring; EMEA 1.05x (€220 million) on PMI/energy; Asia-Pacific 1.22x (¥45 billion ~$300 million +35%) on China 2025/India PLI.

65% of bookings feature NexusEdge platform for 20-30% uptime gains. Backlog $5.6 billion +21% YoY, 9-11 quarters visibility, 40% aftermarket. Q3 expected 1.10-1.15x on EV capex/infra/sustainability; $250 million CapEx for 95% OTD.

Gross margin was 29.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year and 80 sequentially, taking EBITDA margin to 18.7%—highest in five years, ahead of peers like Caterpillar/Deere.

Raw materials (45% COGS): Steel (US HRC) down 15% QoQ to $850/ton but +8% YoY; aluminum -10% QoQ to $2,400/MT, +5% YoY; copper -7% QoQ, +12% YoY. Energy/logistics down 20% QoQ but +25% pre-pandemic. Inflation slowed to 2.5% YoY.

Pricing: 6.2% across ASPs—7% North America new machines, 5% aftermarket (42% margins, 95% uptime); 4.5% EMEA with surcharges; 2-3% APAC via Pune localization. 60% in frame agreements with escalators, driving 4.8% ASP rise, +220 bps over costs.

Net: Price-cost +150 bps, mix +100 bps (electrification 15% mix, 35% margins); volumes +9% shipments, 14% aftermarket, $45 million LIFO; labor -6% via AI robots. North America 32% margins, EMEA 24%, APAC 27%.

Hedged 60% 2024 steel at $780/ton ($120 million savings); value engineering -20% copper; top-10 vendors to 45%. 'Smart iron' IoT boosts 10-15% pricing, 28% recurring services at 50% margins.

Q3/FY24: Pricing +4%, costs -1-2%, raised gross margin to 29.5-30.0%.

Operating expenses were $320 million, resulting in operating income of $220 million. Net income was $150 million, or $1.25 per share.

We are reaffirming our guidance for the full year, with expected revenue growth of 12-14% and EPS of $5.00-$5.50. We are committed to returning capital to shareholders through our $500 million dividend and ongoing share repurchases.

Now, I will hand over to David Chen, COO, for an operational update.

David Chen (COO):
Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we've been focused on streamlining our supply chain and improving manufacturing efficiency. We've implemented several new initiatives that are already yielding positive results, including $300 million in vertical integration for U.S. hydraulic fabs and multi-sourcing in Mexico/Vietnam/Indonesia to cut reliance on China. Capacity at key plants like Peoria and Belo Horizonte is at 92% utilization, with Industry 4.0 rollouts—AI welding robots, digital twins, NexusEdge edge-computing—delivering 6% labor productivity gains and 95% on-time delivery versus industry 82%. We're closely monitoring global supply chain disruptions, hedging commodities, and investing heavily in automation, digital technologies, and electrification to enhance capabilities—think hybrid excavators, battery-electric haul trucks, and IoT predictive maintenance boosting uptime 20-30%. Sustainability efforts, like 30% lower Scope 1 emissions and green alloys, are winning ESG capex. These steps de-risk deliveries and support our $12.4 billion backlog execution.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of rising raw material costs on your profitability?

Sarah Mitchell:
Thanks, Mike. As I detailed earlier, we've navigated price-cost dynamics masterfully, delivering 29.2% gross margins up 210 bps YoY. While steel, aluminum, and copper saw lagged YoY inflation—8%, 5%, 12% respectively—input costs decelerated to 2.5% overall, with QoQ declines of 15%, 10%, 7%. We countered with 6.2% pricing actions: 7% in North America on infra tailwinds, 5% aftermarket, surcharges covering 70% exposure. This netted 150 bps favorability, plus 100 bps from electrification mix and productivity. We've hedged 60% steel, diversified suppliers to 45% from top-10, and engineered 20% less copper usage. Forward, expect continued accretion with 4% pricing and 1-2% deflation, supporting 29.5-30% FY24 margins. Backlog visibility buffers risks like renewed tariffs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen (Goldman Sachs):
What is your outlook for demand in the aftermarket services business?

Johnathan Hale:
Great question, Lisa. Aftermarket remains a high-margin fortress—28% of bookings up 18% YoY, 22% gross margins at 42-50%, and growing faster than equipment. Stickiness from our 95% uptime guarantees, PrecisionAg telematics, IntelliMine AI, and NexusEdge IoT—delivering 20-30% uptime gains—drives subscriptions like FarmConnect up 35%. Electrification aftermarket for hybrids/batteries is accelerating, now 15% segment revenue vs. 5% last year. With $12.4 billion backlog (40% services-weighted), 14+ months visibility, and share gains in mining/construction MRO, we see mid-teens growth persisting on installed base expansion and ESG retrofits. Tailwinds from capex cycles in semis, LNG, data centers keep it resilient even if ag softens.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel (Barclays):
Can you provide an update on your progress in reducing lead times?

David Chen:
Absolutely, Raj. Lead times have compressed meaningfully—from 16 weeks to under 10 for forgings/castings via Mexico/Vietnam multi-sourcing, and 16 weeks overall for modular lines vs. industry 24. Digital twins and $45 million procurement savings optimized modeling; $300 million vertical integration in hydraulics/U.S. fabs de-risks. Peoria/Belo Horizonte at 92% utilization with AI robots cutting labor 6%; NexusEdge/EdgeControl ensures 98% uptime/95% OTD vs. 82% peer average. Pune localization cuts APAC landed costs 8%; Kalgoorlie batteries localize mining. These fuel 1.28x book-to-bill, $9.2-12.4 billion backlog execution, positioning for Q3 $2.9-3.1 billion bookings.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in GlobalForge Equipment Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
